texts.preamble: Da vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa Etc. on 18 July, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 39420/2016 Date of Institution : 07.11.2002 Date of reserving judgement : 09.07.2018 Date of pronouncement : 18.07.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus A-1) Sh. Manohar Lal Wadhwa, S/o Sh. Late Sh Karam Chand M/s Wadhwa Store, Shop No. 128, Guru Nanak Market, Karol Bagh, New Delhi - 5 R/o H No. A 23, Subhdra Colony, Sarai Rohilla, Delhi - 35. A-2) M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand 2284, Med Ganj, Sadar Bazar, Delhi - 06 A-3) Mangat Rai M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand 2284, Med Ganj, Sadar Bazar, Delhi - 06 A-4) Pankaj Gupta M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand 2284, Med Ganj, Sadar Bazar, Delhi - 06 Cc No. 39420/2016 Page No. 1/10 Da vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. A-5) Sachin Gupta M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand 2284, Med Ganj, Sadar Bazar, Da vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa Etc. on 18 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117099120/ 1 Delhi - 06 ... Accused person Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t
texts.facts: he PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 27.12.2001 the Food Inspector Virendra Singh purchased a sample of 'Dal Arhar" a food article for analysis from accused Manohar Lal Wadhwa at M/s Wadhwa Store, Shop No. 128, Guru Nanak Market, Karol Bagh, New Delhi - 5, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No.1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted 750 gms of dal arhar taken from an open gunny bag having no label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh.Surender Kumar, SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after properly mixing the dal arhar with the help of clean and dry jhaba. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles. Each bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa and the price of sample was also given to DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. him vide vendor receipt dated 27.12.2001. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused NO. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa and the other witness Sh N.N. Sharma, FI, Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came (award, as such Sh N.N. Sharma, FI was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. SK/LHA/001142 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartarzine." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Wadhwa Store, Shop No. 128, Guru Nanak Market, Karol Bagh, New Delhi - 5 , at the time of sampling and as such he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.11.2002 alleging violation of section 2i(a)(j)&(m) and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. During the trial, vide order dated DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. 30.04.2010 accused No. 2 M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand, accused No. 3 Mangat Rai, Da vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa Etc. on 18 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117099120/ 2 accused No. 4 Pankaj Gupta and accused No. 5 Sachin Gupta were also impleaded and summoned as suppliers to accused no.1. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned initially and later on other accused were also summoned. The accused no.1 thereafter exercised his option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(b)(j)&(m) of PFA Act and Rule 23 and 29 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh. Virender Singh, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh. Surender Kumar, PW-3 FI Sh. Gian Chand and PW-4 FI Sh. N.N Sharma. PW-1 FI Virender Singh and PW-4 FI N.N. Sharma were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. Surender Kumar. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Dal Arhar" 750 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label or declaration, taking the sample of Dal Arhar and mixing help of a clean & dry jhaba, dividing the sample DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. The accused also made statement Ex.PW1/D alongwith photocopy of MCD Registration Ex.PW1/G. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D on 28.12.2001. The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW1/E, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received, according to which the sample was adulterated because the same was coloured with synthetic colouring matter tartrazine. Thereafter PW-1 collected reply from STO vide Ex.PW1/H. After completion of investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent. The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/J. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/K was filed before the Court by PW-3 FI Sh. Gyan Chand. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/L alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. innocence. Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In their defence, the accused no.1 examined Sh Yograj as DW-1. The accused No. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa also examined himself as DW-2. Thereafter defence evidence was closed vide order dated 10.09.2013 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
